body: In cellular life, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) carries inherited information. Its strands consist of linked units with four common kinds of bases. The bases occur in sequences, and complementary bases can pair so that each strand can guide the copying of the other.

Changes in base sequence are called mutations. Recombination can rearrange existing variation. Inheritance passes some of this information to new cells and to descendants, while genes and environments both influence how organisms develop.

limitations: Genes operate within cells and environments; they do not determine every trait independently.
purpose: Explain inheritance and variation through the roles of DNA.

title: DNA and inheritance
